item.title: From slavery to today: The Black women who shaped America

The New York writer traces three generations of Black women in her family: her grandmother Betty Jean, the daughter of formerly enslaved people in Louisiana who went on to raise eleven children; her mother Connie, who sought a middle-class life in majority-white Houston; and Sasha herself, now raising her daughter Sofia in New York. item.description: Rochelle Ferguson Bouyahi is pleased to welcome Fanny Badache, Researcher at Sciences Po and Lecturer at the University of Geneva. The UN mandate is international peace and security, yet its ability to fulfill that mandate ultimately depends on the cooperation of sovereign states, namely the five powerful permanent members of the Security Council. As the UN is confronted with an increasingly fragmented, volatile and unpredictable international order, Badache argues that when those powers are divided, the mechanisms designed to enable collective security can instead produce paralysis. Temperatures have risen more significantly in tropical areas relative to their historic range than at higher latitudes, including in wealthier countries in Europe and North America. He adds that for Trump voters, if you inflate the risk, people will talk about it and see you're acting. item.description: En marzo de 1974, el Aérotrain I80-HV, obra del ingeniero francés Jean Bertin, alcanzó un récord mundial con una velocidad punta de 430,4 km/h. Lo curioso de todo es que no se trataba de un tren convencional, pues para moverse flotaba mediante un colchón de aire que sus potentes ventiladores generaban al soltar el aire a gran presión sobre una vía de hormigón. A pesar de su proeza técnica e hito cosechado, en julio de ese mismo año, el recién elegido presidente Valéry Giscard d'Estaing puso fin a la financiación del proyecto, respaldando a la SNCF y a sus trenes de alta velocidad TGV… Fuente: Xataka.
